information for citizens to secure access to information under the control of public authorities,

education and knowledge, the attached public safety standard is made available to promote the 
timely dissemination of this information in an accurate manner to the public.

IS: 5846- 1970 







Indian Standard ( Reaffirmed 2002 ) 

SPECIFICATION FOR NAILS, BONE ( SMITH PETERSEN 
AND WATSON JONES PATTERNS) 



1. Scope — Dimensions and other requirements for bone nails of Smith Petersen and Watson Jones 
patterns used as an implant in orthopaedic surgery. 

2. Shape and Dimensions — As shown in Fig. 1 and 2.

IS: 5846 -1970 

3. Material — Any of the materials specified in 3 of IS: 5347-1979 'Specification for general 
requirements of metal surgical implants ( first revision )l 

4. Workmanship and Finish — The nails shall be cannulated. The threads and serrations, wherever 
provided, shall be neat and clean. The edges of the tri-fin at the tip of the nails shall be sharp. The 
nails shall be made in one piece with no riveting or welding. They shall be symmetrical and well 
balanced. They shall be free from cracks, draw marks, burrs, pits r surface contamination and 
impregnated foreign particles. They shall be ultrasonically cleaned, passivated and polished bright to 
give a mirror or satin finish. 

5. Tests 

5.1 Corrosion Resistance Test — According to 6.1 of IS : 5347-1979. 

5.2 Radiological Test — According to 6.2 of IS : 5347-1979. 

6. Marking — According to 5.1 of IS : 5347-1979. 

6.1 ISI Certification Marking — Details available from the Indian Standards Institution* 

7. Packing — The tip of each nail shall be covered with stripable plastic coating. The nails shall then 
be packed individually in polyethylene bags. A number of such pieces may be packed in cartons as 
agreed to between the purchaser and the supplier.
